:root{--bg:#fafaf7;--fg:#1c2421;--mute:#5b6660;--card:#fff;--line:#dfe3dc;--acc:#1f6f5c;box-sizing:border-box;padding-top:env(safe-area-inset-top,0px);padding-bottom:env(safe-area-inset-bottom,0px)}
@media (prefers-color-scheme:dark){:root:not([data-theme="light"]){--bg:#121715;--fg:#e8ede9;--mute:#9aa7a0;--card:#1a211e;--line:#2b3631;--acc:#5fc4a8}}
:root[data-theme="dark"]{--bg:#121715;--fg:#e8ede9;--mute:#9aa7a0;--card:#1a211e;--line:#2b3631;--acc:#5fc4a8}
*{box-sizing:border-box}
body{margin:0;background:var(--bg);color:var(--fg);font:16px/1.6 Georgia,"Times New Roman",serif}
main{max-width:860px;margin:0 auto;padding:40px 20px 64px}
h1,h2,h3,.sans{font-family:system-ui,-apple-system,"Segoe UI",Roboto,sans-serif}
h1{font-size:2.2rem;margin:0 0 4px}
.tag{color:var(--mute);margin:0 0 16px}
nav a{color:var(--acc);margin-right:16px;font-family:system-ui,sans-serif;text-decoration:none;border-bottom:1px solid var(--acc)}
section{margin-top:48px}
h2{font-size:1.4rem;border-bottom:1px solid var(--line);padding-bottom:6px}
.card{background:var(--card);border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:10px;padding:20px;margin-top:16px}
.stat{display:inline-block;margin:8px 20px 8px 0}
.stat b{display:block;font:700 1.6rem system-ui,sans-serif;color:var(--acc)}
.stat span{color:var(--mute);font-size:.9rem}
.ph{border:2px dashed var(--line);border-radius:8px;padding:28px;text-align:center;color:var(--mute);margin:12px 0;font-family:system-ui,sans-serif;font-size:.9rem}
.links a{color:var(--acc);margin-right:14px;font-family:system-ui,sans-serif}
.pill{display:inline-block;border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:99px;padding:2px 10px;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;font:.8rem system-ui,sans-serif;color:var(--mute)}
figure{margin:18px 0}figure img{display:block;max-width:100%;height:auto;margin:0 auto;border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:6px}figure img.map{max-width:520px}figcaption{text-align:center;color:var(--mute);font:.85rem system-ui,sans-serif;margin-top:6px}footer{margin-top:48px;color:var(--mute);font-size:.9rem}
</style>

<header>
<h1>Rafael Vieira</h1>

<section id="crash">
<h2>Severe Crash &amp; High-Injury Corridor Analysis</h2>
<p class="sans" style="color:var(--mute)">ArcGIS Pro | SWITRS, GTFS, LA County centerlines | Summer 2026</p>
<div class="card">
<p>Where do the most serious crashes happen, and how do they relate to places people walk to? I analyzed 99 killed-and-severe-injury (KSI) crashes in Redondo Beach and Torrance (SWITRS, 2021 to 2025) and compiled planning-oriented safety recommendations, presented to faculty.</p>
<div><div class="stat"><b>82.8%</b><span>of KSI crashes within 1/4 mile of a pedestrian generator</span></div>
<div class="stat"><b>Artesia Blvd</b><span>top surface corridor, 10 KSI crashes</span></div></div>
<figure><img class="map" src="data:image/png;base64," alt="KSI crash density (kernel density), Redondo Beach and Torrance" loading="lazy"><figcaption>KSI crash density (kernel density), Redondo Beach and Torrance</figcaption></figure>
<figure><img class="map" src="data:image/png;base64," alt="High-injury corridors by KSI crash count" loading="lazy"><figcaption>High-injury corridors by KSI crash count</figcaption></figure><figure><img class="map" src="data:image/png;base64," alt="KSI crashes and quarter-mile pedestrian generator buffers" loading="lazy"><figcaption>KSI crashes and quarter-mile pedestrian generator buffers</figcaption></figure>
<p><b>Method:</b> kernel density estimation, spatial joins, summary statistics, quarter-mile buffers, and proximity analysis. Schools and parks were digitized by hand.</p><p><b>Key insight:</b> the densest crash cluster (coastal Redondo Beach, driven by pedestrian exposure) is not the highest-count corridor (Artesia Blvd, a wide arterial where speed matters), so each calls for a different safety response. Limits: counts are not normalized by traffic, and bus stops cover so much of the network that transit proximity is a weak test.</p>
<p class="links"><a href="https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33033439/KSI_crash_analysis_report.pdf">Full report (PDF)</a><a href="https://github.com/rafaelVieira3/ksi-crash-analysis">Method and write-up on GitHub</a></p>
</div>
</section>

<section id="heat">
<h2>Los Angeles Urban Heat &amp; Vegetation Analysis</h2>
<p class="sans" style="color:var(--mute)">Google Earth Engine | Landsat 8 Level-2 | Summer 2023 imagery</p>
<div class="card">
<p>How does vegetation relate to land surface temperature across Los Angeles? I built a cloud-masked summer 2023 Landsat 8 composite for the LA area, mapped NDVI and land surface temperature, and averaged temperature within NDVI bins after removing water and very low NDVI pixels.</p>

<figure><img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Average land surface temperature by NDVI bin" loading="lazy"><figcaption>Average land surface temperature by NDVI bin</figcaption></figure>
<p><b>Takeaway:</b> From NDVI 0.2 to 0.7, average land surface temperature fell from about 42 C to about 32 C, roughly 9 to 10 C cooler in the most vegetated areas.</p>
<p class="links"><a href="https://code.earthengine.google.com/ba850374858d7562fbd138c4e956c9fe">Earth Engine script</a><a href="https://github.com/rafaelVieira3/la-urban-heat-ndvi">Code on GitHub</a></p>
</div>
</section>
